papers.title_in_file: YOLOv4: Optimal Speed and Accuracy of Object Detection
papers.version_note: arXiv:2004.10934v1 [cs.CV], 23 Apr 2020. The file is the paper the record names. The text layer holds the paper once, 17 pages.

4.3. Influence of different features on Detector training
4.4. Influence of different backbones and pretrained weightings on Detector training
4.5. Influence of different mini-batch size on Detector training

figures.shows: MS COCO object detection: AP (y, about 30 to 50) against FPS on V100 (x, about 10 to 130); series YOLOv4 (ours), YOLOv3, EfficientDet, ATSS, ASFF*, CenterMask*; a shaded real-time region starts at about 30 FPS; the YOLOv4 series runs from about 43.5 AP at about 65 FPS down to about 38.5 AP at about 123 FPS; the YOLOv3 series is lower, from about 33 AP at about 72 FPS to about 31 AP at about 123 FPS; EfficientDet (D0 to D4) reaches about 49 AP at about 13 FPS.
figures.confirmed_by: YOLOv4 runs twice faster than EfﬁcientDet with comparable performance.

figures.shows: A one-stage detector (input, backbone, neck, dense prediction) drawn inside a two-stage detector (the same parts plus sparse prediction); below it, lists of input, backbone, neck and head examples with citations.
figures.confirmed_by: A modern detector is usually composed of two parts, a backbone which is pre-trained on ImageNet and a head which is used to predict classes and bounding boxes of objects.

figures.shows: Six example Mosaic training images, each a mosaic of four photographs, labeled with augmentation file names.
figures.confirmed_by: Mosaic represents a new data augmentation method that mixes 4 training images.

figures.shows: Three rows compare BN (a batch holds four mini-batches), CBN (cross four iterations, t-3 to t) and CmBN (a batch holds four mini-batches); each row lists, per mini-batch, the accumulate, calculate or normalize steps and, in the last column, the update of W and ScaleShift.
figures.confirmed_by: This collects statistics only between mini-batches within a single batch.

figures.shows: (a) SAM [85]: max-pooling and average-pooling, convolution, sigmoid, then multiplication with the input. (b) Our modified SAM: convolution, sigmoid, then multiplication with the input, with no pooling step.
figures.confirmed_by: We modify SAM from spatial-wise attention to pointwise attention

figures.shows: (a) PAN [49] merges two feature maps by addition. (b) Our modified PAN merges them by concatenation.
figures.confirmed_by: replace shortcut connection of PAN to concatenation

figures.shows: Five example images: (a) Crop, Rotation, Flip, Hue, Saturation, Exposure, Aspect; (b) MixUp; (c) CutMix; (d) Mosaic; (e) Blur.
figures.confirmed_by: bilateral blurring, MixUp, CutMix and Mosaic, as shown in Fugure 7

figures.shows: Six panels, each AP (left column) or AP50 (right column) on y against FPS on x, for Maxwell (top), Pascal (middle) and Volta (bottom) GPUs; each panel shades a real-time region from about 30 FPS and draws the YOLOv4 (ours) series among the compared detectors (the Maxwell and Pascal panels list LRF, YOLOv3, SSD, RefineDet, M2Det, PFPNet, RetinaNet, FSAF, CornerNet, CenterMask, EFGRNet, HSD, DAFS, SAPD, GuidedAnchor, RPDet, Libra R-CNN, FreeAnchor, RetinaMask, Cascade R-CNN, CenterNet and TridentNet in part; the Volta panels list EfficientDet, ASFF*, HarDNet, RetinaNet, SM-NAS, NAS-FPN, ATSS, RDSNet and CenterMask).
figures.confirmed_by: Our YOLOv4 are located on the Pareto optimality curve and are superior to the fastest and most accurate detectors in terms of both speed and accuracy.

figures.shows: Parameters of CSPResNext50, CSPDarknet53 and EfficientNet-B3 (ours) at 512x512 input: receptive field 425x425, 725x725, 1311x1311; parameters 20.6 M, 27.6 M, 12.0 M; average layer output size 1058 K, 950 K, 668 K; BFLOPs 31, 52, 11; FPS on GPU RTX 2070 62, 66, 26.
figures.confirmed_by: Table 1 shows the information of CSPResNeXt50, CSPDarknet53, and

figures.shows: CSPResNeXt-50 classifier ImageNet top-1 and top-5 accuracy for ten feature settings (none; MixUp; CutMix; Mosaic; Bluring; Label Smoothing; Swish; Mish; CutMix+Mosaic+Label Smoothing; the same plus Mish); top-1 runs from 64.5% (Swish) to 79.8%.
figures.confirmed_by: the classiﬁer’s accuracy is improved by introducing the features such as: CutMix and Mosaic data augmentation, Class label smoothing, and Mish activation.

figures.shows: CSPDarknet-53 classifier top-1 and top-5 for three settings: none 77.2% and 93.6%; CutMix+Mosaic+Label Smoothing 77.8% and 94.4%; the same plus Mish 78.7% and 94.8%.
figures.confirmed_by: In addition we use Mish activation as a complementary option, as shown in Table 2 and Table 3.

figures.shows: Ablation of Bag-of-Freebies on CSPResNeXt50-PANet-SPP at 512x512: 17 rows, each a set of ticked features (S, M, IT, GA, LS, CBN, CA, DM, OA) and a loss (MSE, GIoU, DIoU, CIoU), with AP, AP50 and AP75; AP runs from 33.0% (LS alone) to 42.4%; the last two rows, with S, M, IT, GA, OA and GIoU or CIoU, both give 42.4%, 64.4% and 45.9%.
figures.confirmed_by: Further study concerns the inﬂuence of different Bag-ofFreebies (BoF-detector) on the detector training accuracy, as shown in Table 4.

figures.shows: Ablation of Bag-of-Specials at size 512x512: five CSPResNeXt50-PANet-SPP variants (plain, RFB, SAM, SAM-G, ASFF-RFB) with AP, AP50 and AP75; the SAM variant is best on all three.
figures.confirmed_by: including PAN, RFB, SAM, Gaussian YOLO (G), and ASFF, as shown in Table 5.

figures.shows: Detector accuracy (size, AP, AP50, AP75) with different classifier pre-trained weightings: three CSPResNeXt50-PANet-SPP rows and two CSPDarknet53-PANet-SPP rows, all at 512x512.
figures.confirmed_by: Further on we study the inﬂuence of different backbone models on the detector accuracy, as shown in Table 6.

figures.shows: Detector accuracy for mini-batch 4 and 8: CSPResNeXt50-PANet-SPP without BoF/BoS at 608 (37.1 and 38.4 AP) and CSPDarknet53-PANet-SPP with BoF/BoS at 512 (41.6 and 41.7 AP).
figures.confirmed_by: Finally, we analyze the results obtained with models trained with different mini-batch sizes, and the results are shown in Table 7.

figures.shows: Speed and accuracy on MS COCO test-dev 2017 with FPS from Maxwell GPUs (M), batch=1 without tensorRT; columns method, backbone, size, FPS, AP, AP50, AP75, APS, APM, APL; YOLOv4 at 416, 512, 608 compared with LRF, RFBNet, YOLOv3, SSD, RefineDet, M2det, PFPNet-R, RetinaNet, AB+FSAF and CornerNet; real-time rows (FPS 30 or higher) are highlighted.
figures.confirmed_by: Table 8 lists the frame rate comparison results of using Maxwell GPU

figures.shows: The same comparison with FPS from Pascal GPUs (P); YOLOv4 at 416, 512, 608 runs at 54, 43 and 33 FPS with AP 41.2%, 43.0%, 43.5%; compared with CenterMask-Lite, EFGRNet, HSD, DAFS, SAPD, RetinaNet, Faster R-CNN, RPDet, Libra R-CNN, FreeAnchor, RetinaMask, Cascade R-CNN, Centernet and TridentNet.
figures.confirmed_by: Table 9 lists the frame rate comparison results of using Pascal GPU

figures.shows: The same comparison with FPS from Volta GPUs (V); YOLOv4 at 416, 512, 608 runs at 96, 83 and 62 FPS with AP 41.2%, 43.0%, 43.5%; compared with EfficientDet-D0 to D3, YOLOv3 + ASFF*, HarDNet, RetinaNet, SM-NAS, NAS-FPN, ATSS, RDSNet and CenterMask.
figures.confirmed_by: As for Table 10, it lists the frame rate comparison results of using Volta GPU

papers.what_it_is: A 2020 arXiv paper that presents YOLOv4, a one-stage object detector built from a CSPDarknet53 backbone, SPP and PAN neck and YOLOv3 head, with ablations of training features on ImageNet and MS COCO and a speed and accuracy comparison with other detectors.

assertions.value: The authors report that YOLOv4 achieves 43.5% AP (65.7% AP50) on the MS COCO dataset at a real-time speed of about 65 FPS on Tesla V100.
quotes: to achieve state-of-the-art results: 43.5% AP (65.7% AP50) for the MS COCO dataset at a realtime speed of ∼65 FPS on Tesla V100.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Table 10 (p.13) lists 62 FPS on Volta at the 43.5% AP setting, not 65, so the abstract's FPS is a rounded or different figure.

assertions.value: The authors state that they assume the universal features include Weighted-Residual-Connections (WRC), Cross-Stage-Partial-connections (CSP), Cross mini-Batch Normalization (CmBN), Self-adversarial-training (SAT) and Mish-activation.
quotes: We assume that such universal features include Weighted-Residual-Connections (WRC), Cross-Stage-Partial-connections (CSP), Cross mini-Batch Normalization (CmBN), Self-adversarial-training (SAT) and Mish-activation.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's assumption stated without evidence at this point.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use new features WRC, CSP, CmBN, SAT, Mish activation, Mosaic data augmentation, CmBN, DropBlock regularization, and CIoU loss, and combine some of them.
quotes: We use new features: WRC, CSP, CmBN, SAT, Mish activation, Mosaic data augmentation, CmBN, DropBlock regularization, and CIoU loss, and combine some of them
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's statement; the related work (Section 2.2) attributes DropBlock and CIoU loss to other papers.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract calls the whole list new, but Section 2 cites DropBlock and CIoU loss to earlier work, and the acknowledgements credit Mosaic to another developer.

assertions.value: The authors state that the most accurate modern neural networks do not operate in real time and require a large number of GPUs for training with a large mini-batch-size.
quotes: The most accurate modern neural networks do not operate in real time and require large number of GPUs for training with a large mini-batch-size.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim without a citation at this point.

assertions.value: The authors state that they address this by creating a CNN that operates in real-time on a conventional GPU and whose training requires only one conventional GPU.
quotes: We address such problems through creating a CNN that operates in real-time on a conventional GPU, and for which training requires only one conventional GPU.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own aim and scope in Section 1.

assertions.value: The authors state that the main goal of the work is designing a fast operating speed of an object detector in production systems and optimization for parallel computations, rather than the low computation volume theoretical indicator (BFLOP).
quotes: The main goal of this work is designing a fast operating speed of an object detector in production systems and optimization for parallel computations, rather than the low computation volume theoretical indicator (BFLOP).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own goal and scope in Section 1.

assertions.value: The authors state, as their first contribution, that they develop an efficient and powerful object detection model that lets everyone use a 1080 Ti or 2080 Ti GPU to train a super fast and accurate object detector.
quotes: We develope an efﬁcient and powerful object detection model. It makes everyone can use a 1080 Ti or 2080 Ti GPU to train a super fast and accurate object detector.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim; Section 4.5 offers supporting measurements.

assertions.value: The authors state, as their third contribution, that they modify state-of-the-art methods, including CBN, PAN and SAM, to make them more efficient and suitable for single GPU training.
quotes: We modify state-of-the-art methods and make them more effecient and suitable for single GPU training, including CBN [89], PAN [49], SAM [85], etc.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim of contribution; the modifications are described in Section 3.3.

assertions.value: The authors state in the Figure 1 caption that YOLOv4 runs twice faster than EfficientDet with comparable performance.
quotes: YOLOv4 runs twice faster than EfﬁcientDet with comparable performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim from one study; Table 10 gives the numbers.
assertions.reader_inference: Table 10 supports the claim at one pair: YOLOv4 at its second size runs at 83 FPS with AP 43.0%, and EfficientDet-D2 at 41.7 FPS has AP 43.0%.

assertions.value: The authors state in the Figure 1 caption that YOLOv4 improves YOLOv3's AP and FPS by 10% and 12%, respectively.
quotes: Improves YOLOv3’s AP and FPS by 10% and 12%, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim from one study; the caption does not name the input size, GPU or whether the percentages are relative.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper does not state the basis of the 10% and 12% (relative or absolute, which input size). Table 8 lists YOLOv3 at 608 with AP 33.0% against YOLOv4 at 608 with 43.5%, which is 10.5 points, not 10%.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 1: the YOLOv4 series runs from about 43.5 AP at about 65 FPS to about 38.5 AP at about 123 FPS, and the YOLOv3 series is lower, from about 33 AP at about 72 FPS to about 31 AP at about 123 FPS.
quotes: Figure 1: Comparison of the proposed YOLOv4 and other state-of-the-art object detectors.
YOLOv4 runs twice faster than EfﬁcientDet with comparable performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read by eye from a plot.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 8: six panels plot AP (left column) or AP50 (right column) against FPS for Maxwell, Pascal and Volta GPUs, each with a shaded real-time region that starts at about 30 FPS and with YOLOv4 (ours) drawn as one series among the compared detectors.
quotes: Figure 8: Comparison of the speed and accuracy of different object detectors.
Our YOLOv4 are located on the Pareto optimality curve and are superior to the fastest and most accurate detectors in terms of both speed and accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: Layout and values read by eye from a plot.

assertions.value: The authors define as bag of freebies the methods that only change the training strategy or only increase the training cost.
quotes: We call these methods that only change the training strategy or only increase the training cost as “bag of freebies.”
assertions.certainty_reason: A definition the paper gives in Section 2.2.

assertions.value: The authors define as bag of specials the plugin modules and post-processing methods that only increase the inference cost by a small amount but can significantly improve the accuracy of object detection.
quotes: For those plugin modules and post-processing methods that only increase the inference cost by a small amount but can signiﬁcantly improve the accuracy of object detection, we call them “bag of specials”.
assertions.certainty_reason: A definition the paper gives in Section 2.3.

assertions.value: The authors state that a modern detector is usually composed of two parts, a backbone pre-trained on ImageNet and a head used to predict classes and bounding boxes of objects.
quotes: A modern detector is usually composed of two parts, a backbone which is pre-trained on ImageNet and a head which is used to predict classes and bounding boxes of objects.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' general statement of the usual structure, given without a citation.

assertions.value: The authors call the layers that detectors insert between the backbone and the head, and that collect feature maps from different stages, the neck of an object detector.
quotes: Object detectors developed in recent years often insert some layers between backbone and head, and these layers are usually used to collect feature maps from different stages.
We can call it the neck of an object detector.
assertions.certainty_reason: A definition the paper gives in Section 2.1.

assertions.value: The authors list an ordinary object detector as composed of an input, backbones, a neck (additional blocks and path-aggregation blocks) and heads (dense prediction, one-stage, and sparse prediction, two-stage).
quotes: To sum up, an ordinary object detector is composed of several parts:
Input: Image, Patches, Image Pyramid
Dense Prediction (one-stage):
Sparse Prediction (two-stage):
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' taxonomy, given without evidence.

assertions.value: The authors state that after adding the improved version of the SPP module, YOLOv3-608 upgrades AP50 by 2.7% on the MS COCO object detection task at the cost of 0.5% extra computation.
quotes: After adding the improved version of SPP module, YOLOv3-608 upgrades AP50 by 2.7% on the MS COCO object detection task at the cost of 0.5% extra computation.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that in YOLOv3, Redmon and Farhadi improve the SPP module to the concatenation of max-pooling outputs with kernel size k × k, where k = {1, 5, 9, 13}, and stride equals to 1.
quotes: Redmon and Farhadi improve SPP module to the concatenation of max-pooling outputs with kernel size k × k, where k = {1, 5, 9, 13}, and stride equals to 1.
assertions.certainty_reason: A design the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that RFB only costs 7% extra inference time to increase the AP50 of SSD on MS COCO by 5.7%.
quotes: RFB [47] only costs 7% extra inference time to increase the AP50 of SSD on MS COCO by 5.7%.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that the SE module can improve ResNet50 on the ImageNet image classification task by 1% top-1 accuracy at the cost of only increasing the computational effort by 2%.
quotes: improve the power of ResNet50 in the ImageNet image classiﬁcation task 1% top-1 accuracy at the cost of only increasing the computational effort by 2%
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that on a GPU the SE module usually increases the inference time by about 10%.
quotes: on a GPU usually it will increase the inference time by about 10%
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that SAM only needs 0.1% extra calculation and can improve ResNet50-SE by 0.5% top-1 accuracy on the ImageNet image classification task.
quotes: But for SAM, it only needs to pay 0.1% extra calculation and it can improve ResNet50-SE 0.5% top-1 accuracy on the ImageNet image classiﬁcation task.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that SAM does not affect the speed of inference on the GPU at all.
quotes: Best of all, it does not affect the speed of inference on the GPU at all.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that because IoU is a scale invariant representation, IoU loss can solve the problem that when traditional methods calculate the l1 or l2 loss of {x, y, w, h}, the loss will increase with the scale.
quotes: Because IoU is a scale invariant representation, it can solve the problem that when traditional methods calculate the l1 or l2 loss of {x, y, w, h}, the loss will increase with the scale.
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement the paper presents about earlier work, without its own evidence.

assertions.value: The authors state that CIoU loss simultaneously considers the overlapping area, the distance between center points, and the aspect ratio, and that CIoU can achieve better convergence speed and accuracy on the BBox regression problem.
quotes: CIoU loss [99], on the other hand simultaneously considers the overlapping area, the distance between center points, and the aspect ratio.
CIoU can achieve better convergence speed and accuracy on the BBox regression problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that CutMix covers the cropped image to a rectangle region of other images and adjusts the label according to the size of the mix area.
quotes: As for CutMix [91], it is to cover the cropped image to rectangle region of other images, and adjusts the label according to the size of the mix area.
assertions.certainty_reason: A description the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that Lin et al. proposed focal loss to deal with the problem of data imbalance existing between various classes.
quotes: Lin et al. [45] proposed focal loss to deal with the problem of data imbalance existing between various classes.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that label smoothing converts a hard label into a soft label for training, which can make the model more robust.
quotes: The label smoothing proposed in [73] is to convert hard label into soft label for training, which can make model more robust.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors state that post-processing is no longer required in the subsequent development of an anchor-free method.
quotes: post-processing is no longer required in the subsequent development of an anchor-free method.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's statement without evidence in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that the basic aim is fast operating speed of the neural network, in production systems and optimization for parallel computations, rather than the low computation volume theoretical indicator (BFLOP).
quotes: The basic aim is fast operating speed of neural network, in production systems and optimization for parallel computations, rather than the low computation volume theoretical indicator (BFLOP).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own aim in Section 3.

assertions.value: The authors state that for GPU they use a small number of groups (1 - 8) in convolutional layers: CSPResNeXt50 / CSPDarknet53.
quotes: For GPU we use a small number of groups (1 - 8) in convolutional layers: CSPResNeXt50 / CSPDarknet53
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in Section 3.

assertions.value: The authors state that for VPU they use grouped-convolution but refrain from using Squeeze-and-excitement (SE) blocks.
quotes: For VPU - we use grouped-convolution, but we refrain from using Squeeze-and-excitement (SE) blocks
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in Section 3.

assertions.value: The authors state that their objective is to find the optimal balance among the input network resolution, the convolutional layer number, the parameter number and the number of layer outputs (filters).
quotes: Our objective is to ﬁnd the optimal balance among the input network resolution, the convolutional layer number, the parameter number
and the number of layer outputs (ﬁlters).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own objective in Section 3.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that their numerous studies demonstrate that CSPResNext50 is considerably better than CSPDarknet53 for object classification on the ILSVRC2012 (ImageNet) dataset.
quotes: our numerous studies demonstrate that the CSPResNext50 is considerably better compared to CSPDarknet53 in terms of object classiﬁcation on the ILSVRC2012 (ImageNet) dataset
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim; the numerous studies are not shown beyond Tables 2 and 3.
assertions.reader_inference: Tables 2 and 3 are consistent: the baseline top-1 is 77.9% for CSPResNeXt-50 and 77.2% for CSPDarknet-53.

assertions.value: The authors state that CSPDarknet53 is better than CSPResNext50 for detecting objects on the MS COCO dataset.
quotes: However, conversely, the CSPDarknet53 is better compared to CSPResNext50 in terms of detecting objects on the MS COCO dataset
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim; Section 4.4 and Table 6 give the supporting detector measurements.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in contrast to the classifier, the detector requires a higher input network size (resolution) for detecting multiple small-sized objects, more layers for a higher receptive field, and more parameters for greater capacity to detect multiple objects of different sizes in a single image.
quotes: In contrast to the classiﬁer, the detector requires the following:
Higher input network size (resolution) – for detecting multiple small-sized objects
More layers – for a higher receptive ﬁeld to cover the increased size of input network
More parameters – for greater capacity of a model to detect multiple objects of different sizes in a single image
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim without evidence at this point.

assertions.value: The authors report that CSPResNext50 contains only 16 convolutional layers 3 × 3, a 425 × 425 receptive field and 20.6 M parameters, while CSPDarknet53 contains 29 convolutional layers 3 × 3, a 725 × 725 receptive field and 27.6 M parameters.
quotes: The CSPResNext50 contains only 16 convolutional layers 3 × 3, a 425 × 425 receptive ﬁeld and 20.6 M parameters, while CSPDarknet53 contains 29 convolutional layers 3 × 3, a 725 × 725 receptive ﬁeld and 27.6 M parameters.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the properties of its own architectures in Section 3.1.

assertions.value: The authors report in Table 1, at 512x512 input resolution, receptive fields of 425x425, 725x725 and 1311x1311 and parameters of 20.6 M, 27.6 M and 12.0 M, in the order CSPResNext50, CSPDarknet53, EfficientNet-B3 (ours).
quotes: CSPResNext50 CSPDarknet53 EfﬁcientNet-B3 (ours)
assertions.certainty_reason: Table 1 gives the properties of the architectures the paper compares.

assertions.value: The authors report in Table 1 FPS on a GPU RTX 2070 of 62 for CSPResNext50, 66 for CSPDarknet53 and 26 for EfficientNet-B3 (ours).
quotes: CSPResNext50 CSPDarknet53 EfﬁcientNet-B3 (ours)
FPS (GPU RTX 2070) 62 66 26
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that this theoretical justification, together with their numerous experiments, shows that the CSPDarknet53 neural network is the optimal model of the two as the backbone for a detector.
quotes: This theoretical justiﬁcation, together with our numerous experiments, show that CSPDarknet53 neural network is the optimal model of the two as the backbone for a detector.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim; the comparison is between two backbones only.
assertions.reader_inference: The claim is scoped by the text to the two models compared; Table 1 also lists EfficientNet-B3, which the text does not choose between.

assertions.value: The authors summarize the influence of receptive field sizes: up to the object size allows viewing the entire object, up to network size allows viewing the context around the object, and exceeding the network size increases the number of connections between the image point and the final activation.
quotes: Up to the object size - allows viewing the entire object
Up to network size - allows viewing the context around the object
Exceeding the network size - increases the number of connections between the image point and the ﬁnal activation
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's statement without evidence in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that they add the SPP block over CSPDarknet53 since it significantly increases the receptive field, separates out the most significant context features and causes almost no reduction of the network operation speed.
quotes: We add the SPP block over the CSPDarknet53, since it signiﬁcantly increases the receptive ﬁeld, separates out the most signiﬁcant context features and causes almost no reduction of the network operation speed.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim; no ablation of SPP alone is reported in this paper.
assertions.reader_inference: Table 5 holds SPP in every row, so the paper reports no run that isolates the SPP block's effect on accuracy or speed.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use PANet as the method of parameter aggregation from different backbone levels for different detector levels, instead of the FPN used in YOLOv3.
quotes: We use PANet as the method of parameter aggregation from different backbone levels for different detector levels, instead of the FPN used in YOLOv3.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own design choice in Section 3.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that they choose the CSPDarknet53 backbone, the SPP additional module, the PANet path-aggregation neck, and the YOLOv3 (anchor based) head as the architecture of YOLOv4.
quotes: Finally, we choose CSPDarknet53 backbone, SPP additional module, PANet path-aggregation neck, and YOLOv3 (anchor based) head as the architecture of YOLOv4.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own architecture in Section 3.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that in the future they plan to expand significantly the content of Bag of Freebies (BoF) for the detector and sequentially check the influence of each feature in an experimental fashion.
quotes: In the future we plan to expand signiﬁcantly the content of Bag of Freebies (BoF) for the detector
sequentially check the inﬂuence of each feature in an experimental fashion.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state in Section 3.1 what they have not yet done.

assertions.value: The authors state that they do not use Cross-GPU Batch Normalization (CGBN or SyncBN) or expensive specialized devices.
quotes: We do not use Cross-GPU Batch Normalization (CGBN or SyncBN) or expensive specialized devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in Section 3.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that not using SyncBN or specialized devices allows anyone to reproduce their state-of-the-art outcomes on a conventional graphic processor, for example a GTX 1080Ti or RTX 2080Ti.
quotes: This allows anyone to reproduce our state-of-the-art outcomes on a conventional graphic processor e.g. GTX 1080Ti or RTX 2080Ti.
